content.value_statement: React Native teams need reliable patterns for navigation, native APIs, offline data, and mobile releases. This skill provides Expo-based architecture guidance, implementation examples, and production checks.
actual_capabilities: Shows an Expo Router project structure with auth, tab, and modal screen groups.
Compares Expo and bare React Native tradeoffs for native modules and builds.
Provides setup commands for Expo, secure storage, haptics, and AsyncStorage.
Demonstrates authentication flow with SecureStore and protected routes.
Explains offline-first data persistence with React Query and AsyncStorage.
Covers native integrations, performance lists, and EAS build workflows.
limitations: Examples are architectural starting points, not a complete production app.
It does not verify dependency versions against the current Expo SDK.
Native module guidance may still need platform-specific implementation work.
Release examples require valid Expo and app store credentials.

use_cases.title: Start an Expo App
use_cases.description: Create a project structure with navigation groups, shared providers, and initial dependencies.

use_cases.title: Standardize App Architecture
use_cases.description: Define patterns for auth, offline data, native APIs, and platform-specific components.

use_cases.title: Prepare Mobile Releases
use_cases.description: Plan EAS build profiles, store submission steps, and real-device validation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a New App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a React Native app structure for a simple authenticated Expo app.

prompt_templates.title: Design Navigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design Expo Router tabs, auth routes, and dynamic product screens for my app.

prompt_templates.title: Add Offline Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan React Query caching, optimistic updates, and offline recovery for a mobile catalog.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Mobile Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review EAS build profiles, platform differences, and release checks before submission.

output_examples.input: Plan a React Native storefront with authentication and product browsing.
output_examples.output: A screen map with auth routes, tab navigation, product detail routes, and shared providers.

output_examples.input: Improve offline support for a product catalog.
Prepare an Expo app for internal Android testing.
output_examples.output: A release checklist covering preview builds, Android package settings, credentials, and device testing.

best_practices: Use Expo and EAS when they fit the product native requirements.
Test navigation, permissions, and performance on real iOS and Android devices.
Keep secrets out of source code and use secure storage for tokens.
anti_patterns: Running mobile release commands without confirming the target profile and platform.
Treating documentation snippets as complete app code without adapting them.
Storing service account files or API credentials in the repository.

faq.question: Does this skill require Expo?
faq.answer: It is Expo-first, but it explains tradeoffs with bare React Native.

faq.question: Can it create a complete app?
faq.answer: It provides architecture patterns and examples. You still need product-specific implementation and testing.

faq.question: Does it cover navigation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Expo Router stacks, tabs, dynamic routes, and protected auth flows.

faq.question: Does it handle offline data?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows React Query persistence, network status handling, and optimistic update patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with native APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers haptics, biometrics, notifications, and platform-specific code examples.

faq.question: Is it safe to use credentials with EAS examples?
faq.answer: Use local or managed secrets. Do not commit service account files or tokens.
